L1_registration.question: Must an individual register a business to sell digital services/products? Simplest legal form?
L1_registration.answer: Register for a RUC (taxpayer number) with the DNIT. Online registration is available for individuals (personas físicas), and RESIMPLE small businesses have a special route with a scanned ID. When registering, you declare your activity and taxes: a freelancer providing personal services typically declares IVA and IRP (YoFacturo). Older DNIT rules required appearing in person to approve the application and get the Marangatu access key (search summary).

L3_income_tax_foreign.question: Income tax on foreign-source income for residents; rates or special regimes
L3_income_tax_foreign.answer: Paraguay taxes only Paraguayan-source income. Residents' profits from services provided abroad are not taxed unless the service is for a local company paying corporate tax or a person subject to IRP. Remote workers with exclusively foreign-sourced income may owe 0% IRP. Personal-services income (IRP) is taxed at 8%/9%/10% on net income, and an exemption threshold of about PYG 80 million is reported.

L7_incentives.question: Legal incentives / tax holidays / special zones relevant to small digital businesses
L7_incentives.answer: RESIMPLE, the simplified regime for small businesses, applies when annual billing does not exceed PYG 80,000,000. RESIMPLE taxpayers are not VAT taxpayers. A separate SIMPLE regime covers medium businesses. Per the DNIT (search summary, not captured), RESIMPLE has fixed quarterly payments of about PYG 60,000–240,000 and one annual return (Form 502). Whether it suits freelance services was not confirmed.

W1_workarounds.question: Simple, legal routes around payment barriers for a beginner (no misrepresentation, nominees or sanctions evasion)
W1_workarounds.answer: Barriers: Stripe does not accept merchants here; platforms that pay out through PayPal Payouts cannot pay PayPal accounts here (not on PayPal's Payouts list, see P4 for ordinary PayPal receiving); Wise does not let residents hold money. Simple legal routes: (1) Sell digital products or software through a merchant of record: Paddle (software/SaaS only; each seller reviewed), Lemon Squeezy (bank payouts), Polar, Dodo Payments. The platform is the legal seller to your customers, handles card payments and consumer VAT/sales tax, and pays you out. You still declare the payouts as your income at home (see L3). (2) Sell services on Upwork, which is available here (not on its restricted list). Which withdrawal methods you get (bank, PayPal, Payoneer, etc.) depends on the country and shows in your account. (3) Creator income through the YouTube Partner Program (available here). (4) Paid apps and in-app sales through Google Play (merchant registration available here). (5) For direct clients, a bank transfer (SWIFT) into your own local account always works. Follow the local foreign-exchange rules (see P1) and keep invoices. Avoid: opening accounts with a foreign address, a relative's or friend's identity, or a VPN to look like you are elsewhere. It breaches platform terms (accounts and funds get frozen) and can break anti-money-laundering or sanctions law.
